Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00304

The answer is, first, that the philosophers did not deny that any action has an end or purpose. They denied only that God’s action as a whole, and His first act, have some additional goal beyond His own essence. As for the later and particular acts, they affirmed that each has its own end. Their books are full of discussions of the ends and benefits of beings, as can be seen in their studies of the heavens, bodily balances, compound things, anatomy, medicine, and more.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00305

Second, as you have learned more than once, God’s action follows from His own will and approval. The necessity that follows from them is not the same as compulsion in mindless natural causes or forces. Third, even if the objection were right, a philosopher could still investigate how actions follow from their own causes in a fitting way, without contradiction. A philosopher could also ask how evil can come from what is good in itself, and show that what first and directly comes from God is good. Evil does not come from Him directly. Rather, the production of much universal good incidentally leads to a few particular evils. Compared with the great goods, those evils are few. So nothing evil comes from God in itself.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00306

This discussion also answers a major objection from the Magians, who believed in two eternal principles: Yazdan, the source of good, and Ahriman, the source of evil. That alone is a great honor of this inquiry. It also answers the seed of doubt raised by Satan, when he objected to the angels—who are among the noblest beings in the heavens, just as philosophers are among the noblest in the gardens of paradise—by asking God, “Why did You create me, when You knew I would lead Your servants astray and turn them from the straight path?” The answer given—“He is not questioned about what He does”—is decisive as a reply to someone arguing with a person who cannot understand a demonstration. The Qur'an gives three ways to address people: demonstrative reasoning for those who are complete and brought near to God; exhortation for people seeking safety and for the people of the right; and argument to rebut the doubts of those who have gone astray, the people of the left who deny the Day of Judgment.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00307

Another objection says: if philosophers allow a noble being to come from God for the sake of something low—if the world of intellect is created first, then the world of soul through it, and bodily nature through the soul, until the chain ends at matter, which is the lowliest thing—then why do they not also allow what is evil in itself to come from the Good? The answer is that this mistake comes either from confusing a true end with a necessary consequence, or from assuming that the converse of a universal statement is itself universal. It does not follow that because every end is, in one respect, later than the thing directed toward it, everything that is later in that respect is an end. So it does not follow that common matter is nobler than the heavens, or that the heavens are nobler than the active intellects. “End” can mean the purpose for which an action is done, or the point at which a process finishes. One can say that the chain of eternal things ends at common matter, or something like it, and that a series of actions comes to an end.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00308

The divine generosity has no such end. When philosophers say that God brings things into existence in order, from the intellect down to matter, they mean something like the Qur'anic statement, “He directs the affair from heaven to earth.” They do not mean that matter, or anything like it, is the final aim of His generosity. If that were so, existence would not turn back from this lower dwelling and lowest earth toward the highest perfection, in the reverse order of its first descent, as God says: “Then they will return to Him,” and “As We began the first creation, so We shall bring it back again—a promise binding on Us; We will surely do it.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00309

Those who talk at length about good and evil and find the issue difficult are often people who imagine that the vast divine works—the heavens and all they contain—were created only for human beings. They also imagine that God’s actions begin with a choice and aim at goals in the same way as our chosen actions do. If this ignorant person, shut off from the insight of those who know, thought carefully even for a moment, they would see that if things were as they imagine, and there were no firm order and true divine knowledge and rules in place from eternity, then God’s friends would not have suffered such severe trials or faced the power of enemies and oppressors. Nor would God’s enemies—tyrants, impostors, and people of corrupt faith, false beliefs, and wicked opinions—have enjoyed the power to spread their false religions, seize people and property, act arrogantly, and show hostility.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00310

If God’s will were newly formed and arbitrary, what would stop Him from making events fit each person’s desires, especially when that person was one of God’s friends or a righteous servant? Someone could then ask why God, with such a will, did not remove every obstacle and grant the requested good. Why did He not combine safety from harm with reward? Why did He not remove disbelief and oppression from the world so that it would always be filled with justice and fairness? Why did He not make the earth unlike this earth—pure, radiant, and free of the stains of disbelief and sin, as it will be in the next life?
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00311

If they reply that eternal determination prevented this, we ask whether that determination was necessary or only one possibility among others. If it was only one possibility and God chose it, there must be some further reason for that choice, as they themselves maintain. And choosing universal good would have been better, since disbelief does no good for the unbeliever, nor misery for the wretched. If the determination was necessary, so that things could not exist except as they do, then they have conceded that it must be so. If they say, “He does what He wills, and no one may ask why,” we reply that their idea of forbidding the question—because it supposedly burns the tongue, makes inquiry unlawful, or prevents proof from reaching God—is false in every form. If they claim that one cannot ask why about matters known by reason, then an opponent could use that answer to block every proof, including proofs that the world’s features need a reason, or disputes about whether God’s attributes exist. The opponent could simply say, “No one may ask why.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00312

A serious difficulty remains. God is pure good, generous and kind, and has no need of the obedience of the obedient or the sins of the guilty. Why, then, does He punish unbelievers in the next life with fire forever, as the Qur'an says: “They are the people of the Fire; they will remain there forever,” along with other passages that say their punishment has no end? We have already pointed out that a natural kind must, by its nature, reach its own perfection in all its individuals, or at least in most of them, without being blocked forever. As long as a thing remains what it is by nature, it must not be kept forever from its second perfection or from the purpose for which it was made. When a force that holds it back is removed, it must return to that perfection. As the noblest of creatures said, “Each is guided toward what it was created for.” A force that holds something back cannot do so forever.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00313

So either disbelief and the like take a person out of their first nature and make them part of a different kind, or they do not. Either way, eternal punishment seems impossible. If the person leaves their original nature, that is clear: through repeated acts of desire or anger, they become a different kind of being. Their settled character becomes the form of their self and the substance of their nature. Those actions then complete their nature, as satisfying desire completes a beast and overpowering others completes a predator. A being does not suffer from what suits its own nature; rather, it takes pleasure in it, as we see in many people.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00314

If the person remains in the nature they began with, then the barrier that hides that nature from them is accidental and temporary. Once the barrier is gone, they return to their original nature and receive the wide mercy and all-embracing generosity, with no one to prevent it and no veil between them. There is therefore no reason for punishment to last forever.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00315

The answer will become clear in its proper place, God willing, when we explain the different kinds of souls in the next life. In later chapters we will also give an account that points to the breadth of God’s grace and the reach of His mercy to all His creatures, in this life and the next.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00316
VII. Why what people call evils occur in this world
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00317

The eternal will has been directed toward what is good for created beings. No one who truly understands the matter can doubt this, as we will explain when we show that the order of the world, as it is, is the noblest possible order, the most complete and best that can be conceived. This is firmly established, and both philosophers and theologians agree on it, whether they believe in an eternal decree or in a renewed act of choice and an additional purpose. Even someone who believes in choice can say that the world could not be made better than it is. If it could, and the free Creator did not know that a better world was possible, His knowledge would not fully encompass universals and particulars. If He knew and did not make it, though He had the power, that would contradict His generosity, which embraces all beings.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00318

Al-Ghazali says this in one of his books. The complete Shaykh, Muhyi al-Din Ibn al-ʿArabi, quotes him in The Meccan Revelations and approves the argument. It is a sound demonstration. God, exalted in majesty, has unlimited power and complete generosity. Whatever has no matter, needs no special readiness, and faces no opposing force flows from Him simply because it is possible in itself, through creation from nothing. The whole order is one universal kind and one unique form, without matter. Anything without matter has its kind confined to one individual. Its being is therefore not held back by limited readiness or a fixed time; it must be brought into being. So this order cannot be better either as a kind or as an individual.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00319

If this is so, then the basic elements of possible things in this order are revolving spheres and moving stars, moved by higher longings, and elements arranged in sequence. They are ready to produce many other kinds of beings. This can happen only through changes and transformations in the matter of generated things, brought about by the positions and movements of the heavens. A created thing cannot be made dependent on motion while every motion has the same result. Each motion must have a different effect. If the first effect agrees with one thing’s nature, a second effect may oppose it. Nor can the result of one motion, when it suits one nature, suit the natures of all other things. What is better must be given priority.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00320

For example, the sun’s light and heat may act on a place on earth, softening and transforming it until it takes on another nature and produces a kind more noble than the earth itself. This does not suit the earth simply as earth; yet divine mercy calls for it. If the earth could feel, it would know that leaving its present state, though painful and forced from the standpoint of what it is now, brings great kindness beneath that pain and force: it changes from one form into another, nobler and more ready to receive life and divine mercy.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00321

The divine Word points to this meaning: “Come, willingly or unwillingly.” The two said, “We come willingly.” Coming to God—as in death and similar changes—may at first seem unwelcome because a thing is attached to its particular state. But when it passes from that state into another, what it fled from becomes what it seeks, and what it disliked becomes what it desires. Death, decay, and similar things are therefore necessary parts of the order. It would not have been wise to create this world without creating the conditions that entail some evil.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00322

Look more deeply into the secrets of created things, and you will see that the whole is good and well ordered. Death, which people dread, is in truth a passage of the soul from a lower state to a higher one. It is one of the natural forms of completion. Every time nature reaches a fuller state, something comes to be and something less complete passes away. When a seed becomes an animal, for example, the seed’s former form disappears. In the same way, when an animal’s sensory form is completed by a form suited to the afterlife—an imaginal or intellectual form—the sensory form must be shed, and the spirit must leave this natural body.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00323

The innate heat, which those who truly understand regard as a heavenly substance in the hand of an angel who draws out souls and carries them from one state to another, does not by its nature exist merely to dissolve and consume moisture until death occurs. If that were its purpose, God would not have given it to us or set it to work in the body. God permits anyone to die—especially a human being—only so that another life may begin in the world of return. You will learn that the souls of animals, and even plants, also pass to that world. The true work of this heat is to regulate the body’s balance, transform it, and warm its matter into a lighter, finer state, so that it can become a suitable vehicle for the soul: a gentle intermediary body that obeys its rider, rather than a wild one pulled first in one direction and then another because it is made from opposing elements. This change of vehicles prepares the soul to leave this home and journey toward God. In this sense death is natural—not in the sense given by physicians and other naturalists, who say death comes when moisture runs out and the body’s powers fail, as we have already explained.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00324

So every kind of death and decay, the dissolving of forms, and similar things that happen by nature rather than by force or chance, has the cause we have described. There is no evil or harm in a lower form being sacrificed for a nobler one, or in a lower and less complete kind becoming food for a higher, fuller kind. The elements feed compound beings; compound beings feed plants; plants and animals feed human beings. In this way human beings gain honor and excellence, and are prepared for the journey to a brighter realm.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00325
Let us now return to another way of explaining the kinds of relative good and evil that lead to a greater good, following the approach found in some earlier books.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00326
VIII. The relative amounts of good and evil
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00327

Know that good and evil are spoken of in four ways. One concerns the heavens: the good or bad fortunes associated with the stars. Another concerns natural things: coming to be and passing away, and the pains and illnesses that affect bodily balances in animals. A third concerns the nature of living things made from the elements: their conflicts and alliances, their affection and hostility, love and enmity, and the struggle and competition built into their nature. A fourth concerns souls governed by the commands and prohibitions of divine law, and the happiness or misery, both immediate and in the afterlife, that follows.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00328

The good attributed to favorable arrangements of the heavens comes from the care and will of the First Reality. The evil attributed to unfavourable arrangements is accidental, not intended in the first place. For example, the sun may shine on and warm one region for a time, then move away and leave it cool for a while, so that animals and plants can grow there. This happens through the care of the First Reality and the demands of His wisdom, for the sake of the general good and common benefit. God says: “Tell Me: if God made the day last forever over you …” The excessive heat or cold that occasionally kills some animals or plants in certain places and at certain times is not intended in itself.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00329

The good attributed to natural things—the coming to be of animals, plants, and minerals, and the causes that help them grow and reach their fullest state and end—is all approved by God, and comes from the will and care of the Creator who sustains all things. The evils of decay and calamity that befall them after they come to be are incidental, not intended in the first place. They occur as a side effect and consequence.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00330

Since individuals in this world cannot remain forever in matter, divine wisdom and care arranged for their forms and the source of their kind to endure through a succession of individuals. Their nature is preserved by the continual arrival of new examples, even though individual beings are always dissolving and passing away. This is necessary for wisdom and care because there are many great goods and perfections hidden in potential, without end.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00331

They cannot all emerge from potential into actuality at once. Bodily matter cannot receive, all at the same time, every perfection contained within the guiding intellect of a natural kind, the world of its unseen reality, and the source that pours its being into its fixed archetype. It receives these perfections one after another, gradually and through the passage of time. This is true even of one kind of nature; how much more so of all natural lights and their many conditions, qualities, consequences, and effects. If God had created all human beings who ever lived, those alive now, and those who will live until the Day of Judgment at once, the broad earth could not hold them. How, then, could it also hold their animals, plants for food, possessions, and all they need during their lives? For this reason God creates them generation after generation, nation after nation. The earth cannot hold them all, and matter cannot receive them all at once.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00332

This shows that the shortfall lies in matter and its capacity to receive, not in the Creator. An action can fall short because the maker is weak or lacks knowledge, but it can also fall short because the tools and materials needed for skilled work are missing, or because of the limits of place, time, motion, and similar conditions. It can also fall short because of the material itself. Iron is hard to twist into a long cord, unlike hemp or wool; that is not the blacksmith’s failure, but a limit of the iron. Air cannot hold a writer’s letters because it flows away. A carpenter cannot make a ladder that reaches the sky because there is no wood, not because the carpenter is incapable. A wise person cannot teach a child who is not ready to learn; the fault lies in the child’s readiness, not in the wise teacher. Likewise, when some wretched people are not guided by a prophet’s call and warning, the shortfall is not in the prophets, peace be upon them all, or in their ability to guide and warn. Rather, corrupt souls are not ready to receive what would bring them nearer to God and His highest kingdom. The same principle applies to matter’s inability or difficulty in receiving forms: the shortfall is in matter, not in the wise Creator and Director.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00333

There is another reason. These beings begin with the weakest and least complete kind of existence, then gradually rise to their fullest states and ends by means of causes that help them grow and develop. The Creator’s care brings them to their most complete ends. Such causes are called good. Any cause that gets in the way and holds them back is called evil. Yet it is evil only by extension, not in the first place. It is evil in relation to the thing it prevents from reaching its perfection and end, but it may be good in relation to something else, helping that thing reach its own perfection. The first kind of cause was created directly and in itself, not for the sake of the second. So its goodness is essential, while its being evil is incidental.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00334

Now that you understand that an action may fail because matter is incapable or because place, time, motion, or similar conditions are missing, you can see the error in the view of many ordinary people and theologians. They do not understand how matter can be incapable or unable to receive a form, so they blame every shortfall on the wise, powerful, and knowing agent. They may claim that God is unable to do many things, such as remove Satan from His kingdom. Apart from the benefits considered in creating Satan, the failure to remove him comes from there being no other kingdom outside God’s kingdom into which he could be sent—not from any lack of power in the Creator.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00335

They may say that God cannot put the heavens inside a needle. They do not realize that the limit is in the needle and its hollow. They may say that God cannot join opposites, not seeing that the impossibility lies in the opposites themselves.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00336

When asked what is meant by “God has power over everything,” they say the verse is restricted, even though it is expressed universally and explicitly uses the word “everything.” They do not realize that the impossibilities they imagine are not things outside their thoughts and conceptions. The mind imagines certain notions, treats them as names for impossibilities, and assigns them properties only hypothetically, not as settled facts. This is like hypothetical propositions that are not self-evident, as explained in some places in this book.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00337

As for the good found in the animal nature of living things made from the elements—love, pleasure, companionship, eating, drinking, and sexual union—there is no doubt that God placed these in their nature and planted them in their original make-up. They are good by His care and approval, directly and in the first place. The discord, fear, hatred, hunger, pain, thirst, wounds, illness, aches, death, and similar things that befall them come through necessity, as side effects and secondary consequences. God gave animals hunger and thirst, the pleasure of what suits them, and discomfort at what harms them because of His wisdom and concern. These things then become causes of their own ends, bringing their bodies to ruin and their structures to destruction, and their souls to misery, as a necessary consequence.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00338

But the wise Creator’s purpose in bringing animals into existence and shaping them is their survival and well-being. He gave them hunger and thirst to prompt them to eat and drink, replacing in their bodies the nourishing fluids that are continually used up as their bodies dissolve and change. He gave them appetites to draw them toward different foods that suit their bodily balance and needs. He gave them pleasure so they would eat the right amount, neither too much nor too little. He gave them pain when their bodies are harmed, so their souls would protect their bodies from injury for a set time. And some animals eat the carcasses of others so that nothing created is wasted.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00339

My dear friend, know that people have been bewildered by the fact that some animals eat others. They have wondered why God placed this in their nature and gave them the tools needed for it: fangs, claws, sharp nails for gripping, holding, tearing, biting, and eating, as well as appetite, pleasure, hunger, and similar powers. They have wondered too about the pain, suffering, fear, and terror the prey experience when they are killed. When people reflected on this and could not see the cause, purpose, or wisdom, their opinions divided and their schools multiplied. Some said that animals’ domination of and eating one another could not be the work of a wise and merciful creator, and so they claimed that the world had two makers, one good and one evil. Others blamed the stars. Some said it was punishment for sins committed in earlier cycles; these were the transmigrationists. Some called it chance. Others said it was best this way. Some admitted they did not know the cause, while insisting that God does nothing but what is wise.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00340

They said all these things because they were searching for a cause and a wise purpose. They failed to find it because they looked at separate cases and asked about each cause in isolation. One cannot discover the universal causes of things by examining individual cases alone. God’s acts aim at universal benefit and general well-being, even when particular harms and hardships sometimes occur. Consider the laws of the true religious order: the law requires retaliation for murder, and says, “In retaliation there is life for you, people of understanding,” although the murderer suffers death and pain. It also requires cutting off a thief’s hand, which benefits the community as a whole even though it causes pain and harm to the thief.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00341

In the same way, God created the sun, moon, and rain for general benefit and the common good, even though they sometimes harm particular people, animals, or plants. The followers of prophets and Imams may also face hardships and pain when establishing the faith and its laws, especially at first. But the Creator’s purpose in making the faith known and establishing its laws is a general benefit and common good for the countless people who will come after them until the Day of Judgment, and for the many blessings and goods those people will receive. Compared with that, the harm suffered by the Prophet, the Imams, and their pure descendants, peace be upon them all, from the attacks of idolaters and the battles and hardships they faced is small.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00342

Likewise, the effort a believer spends in night prayers, fasting during the day, and performing required acts is slight compared with the gardens, companions of paradise, and God’s greatest approval prepared for them. Since the result is the common good, the hardships are small and particular in comparison.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00343

By the same reasoning, the pain animals feel when they are harmed is not meant as punishment or torment, as the transmigrationists suppose. It is meant to urge their souls to protect their bodies and guard them from injury. Bodies cannot seek benefit or ward off harm by themselves. Without pain, souls would neglect their bodies and abandon them to danger before their lifetimes were over. They would all perish at once in a very short time. For this reason animals, unlike plants, were given pain and the natural impulse to defend themselves—by fighting, fleeing, or taking precautions—so they could protect themselves until a fixed time. Once that time arrives, fighting, fleeing, and taking precautions no longer help. They must yield, even if they feel some pain.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00344

With this in mind, we can say that when God created kinds of land animals, He knew none could live forever. He therefore gave each the longest natural lifespan possible, after which natural death comes, whether they wish it or not. God knows that every day countless animals die on land and sea, in plains and mountains. In His wisdom, He made the bodies of the dead into food for the living, and a material source of their survival, so that nothing created would be wasted. This benefits the living and does not harm the dead.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00345

There is another wise purpose. If the living did not eat the bodies of the dead, the corpses would remain and pile up over the ages, until the earth’s surface and the bottoms of the seas were filled with them. Their smell would pollute the air and cause epidemics, killing the living. What could be wiser than this? By letting animals eat one another, God brings benefit to the living and wards off harm from all of them, even though some feel pain when they are killed or seized. The one that kills or catches them is not trying to cause them pain; it seeks the benefit of eating them or avoids harm by doing so.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00346

Know that when the wise Creator brought beings into existence and arranged created things, He divided them into two groups: those brought into existence all at once, and those formed through generation. He ordered and arranged both. For the first, ungenerated group, He made the nobler cause of the lower being its source, its support, and what brings it to its fullest end. For the second, generated group, the order runs in the opposite direction: they begin with their weakest state and rise toward the noblest and most complete. The incomplete serves the complete; the lower helps and is directed toward the nobler.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00347

For example, an individual plant is lower in rank and condition than an individual animal. So the plant’s body becomes food and material for the animal’s body, and the plant soul serves and supports the animal soul. Likewise, animal souls are lower than the human rational soul, so they serve and support it. And when some animals are more fully formed and complete than others, the less complete animals serve and support the more complete. Their bodies become material and food for the bodies of the more complete, helping them survive and reach their fullest end, since the matter of individual beings is always changing and passing away.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00348

This explains the cause that makes animals eat one another. The further purpose is this: when the wise Creator made the things that come to be, either to bring benefit to animals or to ward off harm from them, He left nothing without benefit or purpose. If He had not made the bodies of animals into food for other animals, those corpses would have been useless and would have caused general harm and destruction, as we explained. As for the pain animals feel when seized or killed, we have already explained that God did not make it to torment and punish their souls for earlier sins, as the transmigrationists suppose. It is meant to urge their souls to protect their bodies from harm and not abandon them to danger before their appointed time.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00349

If you ask why animals love life and hate death, there are several reasons. One is that life resembles lasting existence, while death resembles extinction. Beings naturally love permanence and dislike extinction, since permanence is linked with existence and extinction with nonexistence. These are opposites. God, exalted in majesty, is the cause of all beings and remains forever. So all beings love permanence and long for it because it is an attribute of their cause. An effect loves its cause and the cause’s attributes, and longs to resemble them. For this reason, the sages say that the Necessary Existent is the first beloved, longed for by all creatures, as will become clear, God willing.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00350

A second reason is the pain, suffering, fear, and distress animals experience when their souls leave their bodies. A third is that their souls do not know they can exist apart from bodies. You might ask why their souls are not taught that they can exist without bodies. The answer is that they cannot understand such things. If they did, they would leave their bodies before reaching completion. Then they would remain empty and inactive, without any work to do. Nothing in existence is idle: every existent has its own particular effect. It would not be wise to leave souls inactive and without direction, since the source of all things has never ceased for a moment to direct and preserve the world and its beings. Every day He is at work. If He stopped directing, sustaining, and preserving the world for even an instant, the heavens would collapse, the stars would fall, the world would vanish, and souls and bodies would cease to exist.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00351

Know that when complete and perfected souls leave their bodies, they are either absorbed in beholding eternal beauty, illuminated by the lights of the First, and joined to the ranks of God’s angels who are lost in wonder at the majesty of the First of all firsts; or they are occupied with helping imperfect souls embodied in bodies, so that these may rise from deficiency to completion. The perfected souls themselves can then rise to a higher and nobler state until they join the first group, the pioneers brought near to God. “To your Lord is the final destination.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00352

An example in this life is a loving father or devoted teacher who teaches children and students, bringing them from the darkness of ignorance into the open space of knowledge. The students and children learn and grow; the fathers and teachers also become more complete by bringing into action the knowledge, skills, and wisdom that had been potential in their souls. They imitate the Creator, exalted in greatness and majesty, and follow His wisdom: He is the cause of bringing beings from potentiality into actuality, and from hiddenness into open existence.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00353

The more knowledge a soul has, the more skillfully it works, the better its actions and character, and the more it gives to others, the closer it is to God and the more it resembles Him. This is the rank of angels, who do not disobey God’s commands and do what they are told, seeking the way to their Lord and asking which of them is nearest. For this reason the sages defined philosophy as “becoming like God to the extent human ability allows.” The more a person’s knowledge is true, their work sound, their actions good, their character beautiful, their views right, and their benefit to others lasting, the closer they are to God and the more they resemble Him, for God is so.

passage-en-00354

As for the good and evil attributed to human souls because they are subject to religious commands and prohibitions and to the laws of the divine order, all of them are things that exist. This is true whether they are counted as good—such as prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, almsgiving, urging what is right and forbidding what is wrong, keeping family ties, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, visiting the graves of God’s friends, and other acts of obedience—or as evil and disobedience—such as adultery, theft, gossip, murder, consuming an orphan’s property, injustice, oppression, transgression, and similar sins.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00355

As existing acts, they are perfections and goods for a person’s powers of animal life, not for the person as a human being—that is, not from the standpoint of the rational part. Reason or religious law condemns them only in relation to the rational soul, which is perfected when it restrains the powers of desire and anger and gains mastery over them. It is diminished when it is overpowered by the body and moved by bodily powers. When the soul is moved by what is lower and base, that is misery, distance from God’s mercy, and lack of kinship with His highest kingdom.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00356

If we set aside the effects that these blameworthy acts have on the nobler part of the human being, then in reality and from other points of view—more numerous than that one point of view—what is blamed would turn into something praised, and what is condemned into something commendable. Desire, for example, is blamed; the adulterer and adultery are blamed. But desire itself is a natural power that runs through the soul. It is a shadow of the longing found in the angels brought near to God, who are absorbed in contemplation. Anger, too, is a shadow in human beings of the power of the higher forces that overcome resistance. Each is praiseworthy in itself.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00357

Consider desire. Its true nature is love. As it takes shape in men and women, it preserves the human kind and brings new individuals into the world; it also gives pleasure. In these respects it is a perfection, praiseworthy in itself. Sexual intercourse is likewise a perfection and would not be blameworthy if we set aside the incidental feature under discussion. In all these other respects, blame turns into praise. What remains blameworthy is desire’s failure to obey reason and submit to its guidance. It is blameworthy only when it turns into disobedience to reason and religious law, and leads to broken family lines and inheritance, neglect of children’s upbringing, conflict, disorder, and strife. These are absences that arise from the limits of created things and their shortcomings as possible beings.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00358

In the end, all existence and necessity, and all that belongs to them—activity, completeness, perfection, permanence, joy, love, and pleasure—are good, praiseworthy, and effective. Goodness is the whole of reality. Nothing that exists is truly blameworthy; it is blamed only in relation to something else. Let us now explain this point with the strongest argument and the clearest inquiry.

passage-en-00359
IX. The visible world, like the world understood by the mind, is made as well and as fully as it can be
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00360

We have established that God, the Lord of the world, whose existence depends on nothing else, is free from every kind of deficiency. His existence, which is His own essence and reality, is the best and most complete kind of existence. Indeed, He is existence itself and its reality. Everything besides Him is a flash from Him, a trace, or a shadow. That is why we say He is necessary in every respect and is all existence: all existence belongs to Him. There is no cause for Him, and no existence precedes His. Nothing acts upon Him; He has no matter, form, or subject. He has no end beyond Himself, but is the end of all ends, the source of all sources, the form behind all forms, the reality of all realities, the essence of all essences, and the one who brings all things into being.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00361

Anything that comes from such a being comes from the heart of His essence and the core of His own reality. No additional motive draws Him to act, and no goal beyond Himself makes Him act. The existence of what He brings into being does not add a perfection, honor, joy, delight, benefit, desire for praise, escape from blame, or any other imagined or real advantage. He is free of every deficiency and needs nothing in all the worlds. The existence by which His essence is what it is is the very same existence by which He acts. In Him, being what He is and being the source of all things are one reality and one fact—not as with other agents, whose being and acting depend on two different things. A human writer, for example, is a rational being by one capacity and writes by a separate skill. The sun illuminates the earth and fire burns wood through powers different from what makes them what they are. They therefore depend on added qualities and on something able to receive their effects.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00362

God, exalted in majesty, brings things into being from Himself, not from something ready to receive them; He creates both the recipient and what it receives, matter and form together. So whatever comes from Him, from the very root of His reality, must be the noblest possible being and the most excellent created thing that can be conceived. Nothing is better than it except the sustaining Creator Himself.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00363

Since God knows all things through His own essence in the best possible way—the forms of all things in His knowledge are His essence—things have divine, holy forms of knowledge before they exist in the created world. Every divine existence must be perfectly beautiful and radiant. When the likeness of these forms appears in the created world, it must be as beautiful and noble as a created being can be. And when things are arranged, their order must be the best and noblest possible. It begins with the beings whose existence is most noble, such as the active intellects, then proceeds to what is a little less complete, such as the souls of the heavenly spheres, followed by their imprinted forms, and so on, descending gradually to the least complete and lowest beings. The chain of creation ends there and cannot descend further, because nothing lower is possible. This is the final reach of the order, as God says: “He directs the affair from heaven to earth.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00364

From there, through the mixing of sensory matter, motion, and change, successive natural forms flow into recipients according to their different degrees of readiness and the sequence of movements. Existence keeps rising from the lowest toward the best, and toward nearness to the worshipped One, until it reaches the highest point possible in this ascending chain. As God says: “To Him good words rise, and He raises up righteous action.” Here the order of goodness and generosity reaches its summit, and the circle of existence is complete.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00365

This is the finest way to create: the thing created reaches the good end intended for it. No creator can make anything better than that its end should be God’s own essence, exalted in glory. With this order, the whole world is like one person: its beginning is the Real and its end is the Real. Its form is the form of the Real; indeed, its fulfillment is the Real. It is like a circle whose beginning and end are one point—indeed, the whole circle is that point, flowing from itself, within itself, and back to itself. Glory to His essence, too great for comparisons and beyond the reach of words.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00366
X. In detail, every level of created beings is the best and noblest possible; two approaches, from cause to effect and from effect to cause
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00367
First approach: from cause to effect
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00368
1. Everything in the descending order exists in the best possible way
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00369

Nothing at any level of this chain can be more noble than it is, either as this individual or as this kind, in the respect in which it comes from its creator. First, each kind in this order must be confined to a single individual. Multiple individuals of one kind could arise only through motions, chance events, and incidental features that distinguish and multiply them. But before there are motions and chance events, if some individuals of a kind were distinguished by an attribute belonging to the kind or following necessarily from it, then every individual would equally deserve that attribute. It would be arbitrary for one to have it and another not. If the difference came from something outside the nature of the kind, then there would have to be matter, able to receive outside influences in different ways according to its readiness and reactions. But there is no such matter in the world of origination. So each kind there must be confined to one individual.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00370

Second, the principle of the noblest possible being, whose proof was given earlier, shows that the source of all existence and generosity does not create a lower being while a nobler being is possible. The flow of existence from His generosity must proceed from the more excellent to the less excellent. So He first brought into being the active intellects, the honored forms, the angels absorbed in God, and the overpowering lights: the noblest beings actually possible, given their level. Among those holy beings, the one earliest and nearest to the Light of Lights, exalted in glory, is the most excellent and radiant.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00371

Then come the others in order, down to the final level of this class: the lords of archetypes, or ideal forms of natural kinds, affirmed by Plato and the Platonists. We have revived the teachings of the earlier sages on this doctrine, strengthened it, and defended it by answering doubts and removing objections, with the aid of the Mighty and Wise, as explained before.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00372

The last of these shining intellects is the lord of the archetype of the earth. In the language of Persian sages, he is the mistress of the house of earth, governing the forms of the compound kinds that appear in this world. When the chain of intellects reaches its end in descent, the chain of souls begins with the soul of the outermost sphere, which surrounds the heavens. Next comes the soul of the noblest star, then the soul of each star and sphere in turn, down to the soul of the lowest sphere, the nearest heaven. Beneath these come the forms of the spheres and stars, each as excellent as its existence allows, arranged in the best possible order. Their order reflects the order of the intellects, and each form reflects the intellect corresponding to it, without weakness, failure, fatigue, or exhaustion.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00373

Their bodies are the finest bodies, their shapes the best shapes, and their movements the best movements. First, their simplicity: despite the simplicity of their tangible quality, it contains all the sensory qualities in a finer, purer, and more delightful way. In that one quality are all delicious tastes, pleasant scents, beautiful colors, and uplifting sounds. Second, they are spherical, and elsewhere we have shown that the sphere is the best of shapes. Third, their movements are loving and yearning. Their movers are divine beloveds, intellectual angels, and soul-like powers. The first kind of mover moves as an end, without itself moving—like the beloved moving the lover, or a teacher, or knowledge itself, moving the learner. The second kind moves as an agent acting directly, through renewed desire—like longing moving the one who longs, thought moving the thinker, or new knowledge moving the learner. Each of these movers is itself moved.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00374

In short, their movements are the finest, for they are acts of worship directed to God and rites of the intellect. Longing and love for God stir them. Each heavenly being has its own beloved intellect and its own mover, drawing it toward that guide so it can follow and imitate it. Yet all long for the beauty of the Lord of the Worlds and dance in the joy they receive from union with the First of all firsts. With each moment, their movement brings a new longing and delight. A fresh holy influx reaches their being, and another movement follows, carrying them to another longing and pleasure, and so on without end.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00375

From them flow the perfections and goods suited to this world: direct, reflected, and bent rays of light. These prepare matter to receive the forms and perfections that the Active Source pours into it at every moment, until God inherits the earth and all who are upon it.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00376
2. The beings and generated things that rise through the world of composition are perfectly ordered
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00377

The order of beings in this world depends on the movements and positions of the spheres. The order of the spheres, in turn, reflects the order of the divine decree, which you have learned is complete and perfect. It has also been shown many times that these beings do not come from luck or chance, as Democritus claimed; from arbitrary acts of will, as the Ashʿarites supposed; from an incomplete will and an extra purpose, like our own wills, which depend on motives outside us; or from a nature unaware of itself, let alone aware of what it brings about, as the materialists and naturalists claimed. Rather, the intelligible order that philosophers call providence gives rise to the order we see. So this world has the greatest good and excellence possible.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00378

It follows that, in relation to their causes and principles, nothing in this world is arbitrary or accidental. Everything is necessary and natural in relation to the nature of the whole, whether it happens naturally by itself, as a stone falling down; by force, as a stone driven upward; or by choice, as an animal moving across the earth. Everything that occurs in the world of generation must arise from a cause, for a thing does not exist until its existence is necessary. The chain of causes rises to one source, from which things follow in the way He knows, through His wisdom and care. Nothing that exists is out of keeping with the nature of its causes, which lead back to the One who is truly Real. An effect is suited to its cause; it flows from that cause.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00379

So movements that seem to conflict are harmonious and ordered when seen as parts of the whole. Even an extra finger is natural in the nature of the world as a whole, and every lifespan is natural in relation to the whole, even if it is not natural in an absolute sense. Suppose you could know each thing through its causes. Suppose your intellect could leave this dark abyss and journey to God and His kingdom. You would witness the wonders and order of the heavens, then rise to the higher kingdom to see the wonders of divine power and know the First Source truly. You would travel through the Real and from the Real back to creation. In His light, you would see the angels who know, then the angels who act by God’s command. You would also see the powers and natural forces of the heavens that move them, and the causes and principles guiding their movements, longings, forms of worship, lights of obedience, and closeness to God. You would see how these bring about changes in the elements and combine them, and how the forms of generated things and the souls of their changing bodies follow. You would then see all things as beautiful, noble, and pleasing, and know through direct experience what you now know through argument. One like you would truly belong among the people of God’s good pleasure and find the joy of paradise.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00380
3. The world as a whole, in kind and in individual reality, has the best order and fullest completion
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00381

First, the whole world, considered as a whole, is one individual with a natural unity. Its unity is not like a collection of different things that happen to make one object by joining together, as bricks make a house or individuals make an army. The parts of the world have an intrinsic connection because they are arranged as causes and effects, from the noblest to the lower, from the higher to the lowest. A whole arranged in this way has an essential unity. You know that a cause completes its effect, and what is more noble completes what is less noble. A thing is more truly one with itself when it is complete than when it is treated as separate from itself; its parts therefore form one unity.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00382

For us, the world’s unity as one individual is established by demonstration. Aristotle the Sage explicitly said that the world is one living being, and that the questions “What is it?” and “Why is it?” have one answer. Whoever knows what it is knows why it is. If this is so, the ultimate goal of the whole world—called by the mystics the Great Human—is the First Reality, exalted in glory. He answers the question “Why does this Great Human exist?” If the answers to “Why?” and “What?” are one, then God is what completes its essence and establishes its reality. No possible reality can be conceived as higher than one whose whole existence and essence are completed by the First Reality. The whole world, then, is the best and noblest possible.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00383

Let us explain this more fully. If the entire world is one individual, it cannot be replaced by another order, whether that order were better than it or equal to it. Any proposed alternative would either differ from the existing order and fail to belong with it to the same kind, or would not differ from it. Neither possibility works, so no other order can be conceived.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00384

The first possibility fails because it is impossible for there to be substances or attributes different in kind from those in the existing world. The intellects, universal souls, forms of the spheres and stars, and their matter cannot have different kinds of counterparts at the same level. Each comes from its source through a single necessary way of acting, without any contribution from another thing such as matter. Body, simply as body, does not differ in its essential reality. The simple kinds of body differ through their specific forms, which come from intellectual sources by necessary modes of action, either directly or with help from earlier forms. Incidental events have no part in this, since these forms precede motion and readiness. The attributes of simple bodies depend on and are sustained by their substances. If the subjects and the necessary conditions of action and reception are the same, different attributes cannot result. What applies to simple beings applies equally to compound beings and their specific forms, which depend on their matter, combinations, readiness, and necessary attributes, such as the movements and positions of the spheres.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00385

If no substances or attributes other than those that exist could come about, then any other world would have to share this world’s essence and differ from it in no essential respect. The second possibility—that another world could have the same essence but still be a different world—also fails for several reasons. First, whatever has no matter and no prior motion is brought into existence through creation. Such a thing does not vary because of outside conditions, so its kind cannot multiply into individuals. Each kind must be one individual, since whatever distinguishes it is its own essence or something that follows from it, and neither can be multiplied. Second, its existence comes from God’s own essence, with no other source; one cause gives rise to one effect. Third, its individuality comes from God, exalted in majesty, who is individual through His own reality. Every effect is likewise made individual by its immediate, producing cause. It therefore cannot be multiplied. Fourth, God’s knowledge of the good order—which is identical with His essence—requires the world’s existence, so no other world is possible. Finally, as already indicated, the final cause of the world’s existence is the essence of the Highest Source. The cause of its beginning is also the cause of its completion. Anything whose end is the most noble of all things is itself the noblest possible being.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00386
1. A question and further examination
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00387

You may say: if the whole world, the Great Human, is one individual and the noblest possible being because the cause of its beginning and its completion is one and the same—the Real—then the same must be true of the First Effect. It would be like the world in its reality. But then two things would come from the One Real at the beginning of creation, which is impossible. It would also mean there were two beings of one kind above the world, contrary to the principles of philosophy.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00388

The reply is that there is no real multiplicity here. As we established earlier, a thing’s full reality comes from its final defining feature: its form, which grounds all its other meanings. You know that a thing is what it is because of its form, not its matter. What comes from God is one thing: the Great Human, the world as one individual. But it can be considered in two ways, as a whole or in detail. The difference between the whole and its details is in how we understand them, not in what is understood.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00389

If you consider the world as one reality, you judge that it comes from the One Real in a single act of creation. If you consider its details one by one, you judge that what comes first is its noblest and most complete part, the First Intellect. As we have said, intellect is all things. Then the other parts follow one by one, in order from nobler to lower and more complete to less complete, down to the weakest and lowest form of existence. So the Great Human and the first created being are one in their essence and reality. To say “the First Intellect” is, in a sense, to say “the whole world”; and to say “the whole world” is, in a sense, to say “the First Intellect.” There is no difference in their essential or causal standing; the only difference is between the whole and its details.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00390

If you ask how God created the entire world all at once when some of its parts exist gradually, such as times and movements, while others exist all at once, and still others belong to neither class, we reply that the world has another kind of unity, one that gathers and contains all its individual unities. All movements, changes, bodies, and bodily things are included within that unity, as those firmly grounded in knowledge understand. God knows best.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00391
Second approach: from effect to cause
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00392

We see that beings are connected to one another and benefit from one another. Everything incomplete turns toward its own completion, and everything low seeks to join what is higher, by an instinct and natural impulse placed within it by God. We also see the care each higher thing shows for what lies below it, the concern each stronger being has for the weaker, and the way every soul and intellect directs what is entrusted to it with wise guidance, careful shaping, excellent ordering, and gentle completion. Each is brought to the fullest state possible for it.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00393

Form completes matter by giving it measure, shape, and qualities suited to it. If matter is already in its proper place, form lets it rest there; if it is outside that place, form moves it there by the easiest and shortest route. The soul completes the body’s nature by giving it powers and tools, and by giving it the shapes and organs it needs. It preserves the individual for as long as possible and brings it to full growth through nourishment and development. It preserves the kind by producing more of its kind, and keeps the body healthy by maintaining its balance. These functions are carried out through innate heat, which ripens, cooks, and digests matter, removes harmful waste, and retains the healthy blood and other fluids that nourish and sustain the body—phlegm, yellow bile, black bile, and the rest. It also gives the organs their appropriate forms, shapes, sizes, and positions, and arranges them in the best order. Much more could be said; anatomy and the study of the heavens show it. All this happens by God’s permission and inspiration, as He says: “By the soul and the One who formed it, then inspired it with its wickedness and its mindfulness of God.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00394

Intellect likewise perfects, straightens, refines, and purifies the soul from material impurities and bodily stains. It gives the soul knowledge and wisdom, lights it with understanding and guidance, brings its undeveloped abilities to full realization and carries it from darkness into light, strips away its bodily coverings, and raises it from decayed graves and crumbling resting places to the world of resurrection, where it stands before God. The care, guidance, creation, kindness, mercy, generosity, and grace of the First Reality toward the intellect, soul, nature, and all other things are greater than all of this. Let us now explain the point in more detail.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00395
XI. A few signs of God’s wisdom and care in creating the heavens and earth
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00396

Even the finest human minds cannot fully grasp the realities of heaven and earth, the subtlety of their design, the wonders of nature, or the signs of care and wisdom found in them. Most people cannot even fully understand the soul that is their very self: its many states, how its powers work through the body’s senses and organs, how the organs are arranged and shaped, or what each part does and what its purpose is. What anatomists have discovered through careful thought is only a little compared with the subtle features, wonders, and wisdom in God’s design that remain beyond their notice.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00397

If we cannot fully understand our own soul and body, how could we grasp everything in the physical and spiritual worlds? We cannot even examine the true nature of most things that exist, let alone understand them all. Yet, despite this natural limit, while we are strangers in this world, we must still reflect on the wonders of creation and the marvels of nature. God calls us to do so: “Have they not reflected within themselves?” and, “Have they not looked into the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that God has created? Perhaps their appointed time is near. What message after this will they believe?” He says: “In the creation of the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers,” and: “Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, with no gaps in it? And the earth We spread out, setting firm mountains upon it and bringing forth every lovely kind of plant—a sight to behold and a reminder for every servant who turns back to God.” He praises those who reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth, and condemns those who turn away from its signs: “How many signs there are in the heavens and the earth, yet they pass them by and turn away!” And He says: “Woe to every lying sinner who hears God’s signs recited to him, then persists in arrogance as though he had not heard them. So give him news of a painful punishment.”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00398

We must therefore offer a few examples of the wisdom found in the physical world and of the harmony and fine order of its parts. From them we may learn something of the Maker’s greatness, the breadth of His mercy, the abundance of His generosity, and the subtlety of His care.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00399

Think, then, you who are intelligent and attentive to God’s work and the signs in His Book. The Maker’s power to give goodness and mercy is without limit. His generosity cannot stop at some boundary, leaving the endless possibilities beyond it unrealised. That would be impossible. Yet the proofs show that an infinite number of beings cannot all come into existence together, all at once. They must come to be one after another. So God’s work must include a substance through which new and changing things can continue to come from Him, while His own being remains far above change. That substance must have an unlimited capacity to receive what comes from another, just as God, exalted be His name, has an unlimited power to act independently.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00400

Since new events arise as things become ready to receive them, this requires something that changes by nature and comes into being in itself. Its own changes and coming to be can then give rise to new events and to changes in what changes, linking these events to the timeless, unchanging Maker. Out of His generosity, He brought into being noble, luminous bodies whose natures change and whose movements—of their own souls, by nature, and in relation to one another—never cease. Their movements serve higher spiritual purposes and wise intellectual ends. These ends bring forth physical lights and visible forms, which prepare matter to receive an endless variety of forms. In this way, an agent with unlimited power to affect things gives its gifts to a receiver with unlimited capacity to receive them, so that goodness may continue to flow and blessings may never cease. As God says: “If you tried to count God’s blessings, you could never number them.” The Sustainer, who knows the unseen, does not withhold His gifts. He gives to every prepared receiver according to its readiness. Even tiny ants, lizards, and geckos would receive rational souls if they were ready for them.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00401

You have learned that the noblest beings connected with matter and bodies are rational souls. All the rational souls that could exist cannot become actual at once: not with bodies, for that would require bodies and dimensions without limit, and not without bodies, since souls first come into being through their connection with bodies. Matter has an endless capacity to become ready, through successive cycles and periods, to receive the flow of souls from the intellect separate from matter. Those souls that reach completion return to the intellectual world, their true home. Those that do not reach completion remain for a shorter or longer time in some level of the in-between world of images, according to how thick or thin the veil is and how many or few wrongs they have committed.
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00402

Now consider how the heavenly bodies are arranged for the benefit of earthly things. If all of them shone with light, their brightness would burn up the material of everything that comes to be. If none of them shone, the world below the heavens would be left in deep darkness, under a long, desolate night. If their lights stayed still or followed only one circular path, they would have too great an effect on some places and too little on others. If they had no swift movement, they would have the effects of stillness. If the stars did not have a shared swift motion as well as slower individual motions, and if the circles followed by the slower movements did not tilt away from the path of the swift movement, their influence would not spread north and south across the earth. Their benefits would not reach all its regions. And if the sun’s path did not differ in this way from the path of the swiftly moving heavens, there would be no four seasons. The seasons bring about generation and decay and bring the climates and regions of the earth into balance. The divine Book points to this when it says: “Say: Have you considered? If God made the night last forever until the Day of Resurrection, what god besides God could bring you daylight?” Then it says: “Say: Have you considered? If God made the day last forever until the Day of Resurrection, what god besides God could bring you a night in which to rest? Will you not see?”
Kind One: Harm suffered directly from the harmful thing
passage-en-00403

The moon acts as the sun’s deputy, helping ripen and break down things. So its path was made to differ from the sun’s, moving north and south across the seasons. In winter the sun is to the south and the moon to the north, so that neither of their functions is lost; in summer it is the other way around, so that their heating effects do not combine. Since the sun’s path moves north in summer and south in winter, its farthest point from the earth was placed in the north and its nearest point in the south. Its greater distance offsets the heat and light when it moves north, so they do not become too strong; its nearness offsets its southern position, so that its heating power does not become too weak. See how God gave the stars, along with their shared swift movement, other slower movements that carry them north and south along paths that differ in size, speed, and distance from the earth, depending on their farthest and nearest points. Their differing conditions serve created things and the order of the world. God says: “The sun, the moon, and the stars are made to serve by His command”—that is, they follow the paths He has set for them, rising and setting, sometimes moving north and sometimes south.
